new_value:
STALE -- already resolved, in the direction the bead recommended, and at both layers.

The bead offered two options and recommended the strict one ('if doc wins, recommended for security conservatism: add if target.is_internationalized guard on the SmtpUTF8 branch'). That guard is present in pkix-identity/src/lib.rs's san_entry_matches_mailbox:

    GeneralName::OtherName(other)
        if target.is_internationalized && other.type_id == OID_SMTP_UTF8_MAILBOX =>

with the RFC 8398 §3 rationale inline. So the doc and the code now agree, strictly, and the two SAN forms really are disjoint identity spaces as the rustdoc claims.

Tested in both directions: ascii_target_does_not_match_smtputf8_san, internationalized_target_does_not_match_rfc822_san, review_ascii_mailbox_must_not_match_smtputf8mailbox_san (which uses alice@evil.com against a cert constrained to example.com), plus mixed_mailbox_san_matches_ascii_path / _utf8_path for a cert carrying both forms. 94 pkix-identity tests green.

The severity was higher than 'documentation disagreement' suggests, and the regression test says why: 'Combined with pkix-path ignoring otherName for rfc822Name name constraints, this lets a CA constrained to example.com mint a working S/MIME identity for alice@evil.com.' A name-constraint bypass, not a cosmetic inconsistency.

That second half is fixed too, which the bead could not have known: pkix-path now checks otherName(SmtpUTF8Mailbox) against rfc822Name constraints per RFC 8398 §6 (see lib.rs:2521-2522 and 4136-4137). So the bypass is closed at the matching layer AND at the constraint layer rather than relying on either alone.

Found while answering a question about what blocks authenticating arbitrary S/MIME mail -- this was the one open bead bearing directly on From:-header-to-certificate binding, and it turns out not to block anything.
